# NOTES: *The Mystery of the Peacock's Eye* (Brian Flynn; John Hamilton Ltd, London, July 1928; Gutenberg #75195)

## Contents (27 chapters)
I Hunt Ball at Westhampton; II Mr. Bathurst Receives a Distinguished Visitor; III Chief-Inspector Bannister Gets a "Busman's Holiday"; IV A Case of Identity; V John Martin's Evidence; VI Mr. Bathurst Changes His Destination; VII Gentlemen and Players; VIII Daphne Draws Up the Blinds; IX Mr. Bathurst Looks at a Pair of Shoes—and a Luggage-Wagon; X A Room Is Ransacked at "Rest Harrow"; XI A Newspaper and a Second Suit-Case; XII Mr. Bathurst Listens to a Little Local Gossip; XIII Re-enter Mr. X; XIV The Peacock's Eye; XV Alan Warburton Leads Trumps; XVI Of Which Mr. Bathurst Holds the Ace; XVII Bannister Strikes the Trail; XVIII That Leads Round the Mulberry-Bush; XIX Ronald Branston's Story; XX "Findings—Keepings"; XXI The Lord Lieutenant Goes Back a Few Years; XXII Gallant Mr. Bathurst; XXIII Mr. Bathurst Forgets His Change; XXIV What Did Mr. Bathurst Whisper?; XXV Mr. Bathurst's Patience Is Rewarded; XXVI Rendezvous; XXVII Sir Austin Kemble Removes His Hat.

## Ch I – Hunt Ball, Westhampton (February, prior year)
- Red Ruritanian Band. Rumoured Royalty present (Crown Prince, incognito).
- Mutual Bank frauds; Sir Felix Warburton (director) arrested.
- Sir Matthew Fullgarney, Lord Lieutenant; wife Lady (Pauline) Fullgarney. Sir M asks who "Mr. X" is; no answer.
- Major Carruthers, Chief Constable, with tall unnamed man "Mr. X" (incognito, "peculiar position with regard to Society").
- Sheila Delaney: auburn "Burne-Jones" hair; only child of late Colonel Delaney (Westhampton Regiment; drowned 1917 on leave from Gallipoli); mother died ~3 yrs later; old nurse-companion since birth; lives at Tranfield.
- Alan Warburton, nephew of Sir Felix, is Sheila's dance partner.
- Carruthers introduces Mr. X to Sheila. She: "I'm dancing with… the Crown Prince of Clorania?" Mr. X: "You must possess your soul in patience." Her eyes flecked green.
- Carruthers: "where's young Warburton?"
- Carruthers drives Sheila home; newsboys: "Suicide of Sir Felix Warburton—in his cell."
- Next March Carruthers killed in skid/overturn, wet night. Sheila never rode with him again.

## Ch II – Anthony Bathurst
- Bathurst's flat; letter from "Hotel Florizel, W." (cream laid, florid "German-looking" capitals T, B, Y).
- Visitor 11:38 (Rolls-Royce, chauffeur). Calls self "Mr. Lucius". Is **Alexis, Crown Prince of Clorania**; marrying **Princess Imogena of Natalia** in December.
- Bathurst's Trichiniasis/nematode quip; visitor angered.
- Five blackmail letters (9 weeks old to June 22). Demand **£50,000** by **9th of next month**; payment via "Agony Column" of *The Times*. Threat: tell Princess.
- Letter 1 (April 23, Tranfield postmark): "my gay and gallant lover…" Photo of Crown Prince + lady taken at **Seabourne**, **Hotel Cassandra**, last summer, by **Captain Willoughby** (possibly). Lady unnamed.
- Crown Prince visited Westhampton once: Hunt Ball, a year ago last February. Never Tranfield.
- Bathurst: "What happened exactly at the Hunt Ball?"
- Crown Prince's solicitors: Merryweather, Linnell and Daventry.

## Ch III – Bannister at Seabourne (July)
- Chief-Inspector Richard Bannister, "Dandy Dick", of "Big Six". Holiday at Seabourne; horn-rimmed glasses; a month's vacation.
- Captain Willoughby (tall, white teeth; cigarettes) chats with him on lawn of Cassandra.
- Maid summons: Sergeant Godfrey (County Police, Seabourne).
- Murder at **Ronald Branston's** dental surgery, corner of Coolwater Avenue and Lower Seabourne Road (Froam direction, 8 miles). Phone 2:20pm.
- Branston: young lady extraction ~2pm; local anaesthetic; left alone; went to work-room (12 yds across landing) ~2:30 for artificial teeth; bolted in brass bolt outside; 7–8 min. Housekeeper **Mrs. Bertenshaw** released him.
- Victim dead in chair, tumbler on stand. Hydrocyanic (prussic) acid, bitter almonds.

## Ch IV – Identity
- Godfrey: no ID. Bannister: "fingering his chin". Godfrey's cousin at Yard told Godfrey Bannister was here.
- Doctor Renfrew (divisional surgeon; tall, thin, nervous, gold spectacles, watery eyes): hand-syringe from front; large dose.
- Victim: early 20s; cedar-brown three-piece suit (jumper, skirt, sleeveless coat); striped jumper; brown semi-brogue shoes; no jewellery; hat (pull-on waterproof felt, pleated crown, turned-down brim, maker **Moore, Knightsbridge**); gloves.
- Branston's account (lost appointment with **Jacob Morley**, turf accountant, 2:30; Morley never seen).
- Godfrey: insufflator/fingerprint powder on glass and bolt. Mrs. Pearson (female searcher) to be called.
- Phone: **Lauderdale Hotel** thinks they can identify her.

## Ch V – John Martin's Evidence
- **Maynard**, manager of Lauderdale Hotel (florid, cigar). **John Martin**, reception clerk.
- Phone booking Wed 10:50pm for **Miss Daphne Carruthers**, arriving Thursday.
- Thu ~1:30pm girl in car, gave suit-case, room **66**, said back in an hour; drove toward **Froam**. Never returned.
- Martin identifies body.
- Suit-case: "Daphne Carruthers, 11, Lexham Gardens, Kensington" labels (tie-on). Contents: clothes, toilet items; no letters.
- Bannister takes case; plans Press.
- Bathurst introduced: "Mr. Anthony Lotherington Bathurst", 109 miles from Tranfield.

## Ch VI – Bathurst Changes Destination
- Telegram: "Come at once to Hotel Cassandra, Seabourne" from "Mr. Lucius".
- Press: "Young Lady Murdered in Dentist's Chair"; "Lauderdale".
- Crown Prince agitated: followed by two men (small two-seater); letter from "the lady" ("Dear Alexis"; signed pet-name): demands photo return; meet at Cassandra; he met her next day; she left Wed evening.
- Crown Prince names victim: **Daphne Carruthers**. He burned letters with her in wood off road to Froam. Photo "destroyed".
- Crown Prince: Sir Austin Kemble (Chief Commissioner) has authorised Bathurst.
- Bathurst: Morning Message says Lauderdale; Crown Prince insists error.
- Phone call: "I'm speaking to Daphne Carruthers."

## Ch VII – Gentlemen and Players
- Daphne on phone: left Seabourne 10:03pm Wed; Victoria 11:15; Lexham Gardens 11:35pm; phone rang while she was out; police called early Thu; she is alive.
- Daphne arrives by fast train; Bannister met her.
- Police station: suit-case in cupboard; labels are Daphne's; clothes are Daphne's.
- Bannister's theories: exchange by porter; dead girl stole case.

## Ch VIII – Daphne Draws Up the Blinds
- Daphne: suit-case left Wed evening with porter; tipped him.
- Bathurst asks if labels tied same way (yes).
- Daphne's friend **Lois Travers**, 44 Crowborough Mansions, Maida Vale; **fiancé = Captain Willoughby**.
- Bannister theory: victim is Lois Travers. Bathurst: Crown Prince/Willoughby link.
- Willoughby identifies: not Lois Travers.
- Daphne identifies victim: **Sheila Delaney**.

## Ch IX – Shoes and Luggage-Wagon
- Daphne: uncle Major Desmond Carruthers (Chief Constable, Westhamptonshire; d. March last year, motor accident). Sheila's home: **Rest Harrow, Tranfield, near Westhampton**. Sheila's nurse-companion: name "Carr"? Daphne can't recall nickname.
- Bathurst's magnifier: dust on hat (Westhamptonshire vs Marlshire shades), shoe wear → she drove far.
- Hotel luggage: Thursday morning wagon empty.
- Bathurst: suit-case theft = murderer's motive for non-identification. Bannister: "I prefer… data in front of me."

## Ch X – "Rest Harrow" Ransacked
- Train via Bletchley; change at Westhampton; Tranfield branch line (20-min service).
- Station master directions. **Sergeant Ross** (Westhampton man, a year in post).
- Bannister breaks pane; enters via kitchen.
- Postcard (on mat): "4, Rolle Cottages, Otterton. July 3rd. Dear Miss Sheila…" signed "Pinkie", Budleigh Salterton view.
- Bedroom ransacked (drawers on bed). Key in lock of bedroom door (only one open).
- Hand-bag: visiting card "Alan Warburton, 19, Crossley Road, Westhampton"; reverse "Ronald N. Branston—Dental Surgeon—Coolwater Avenue, Seabourne".
- Bathurst: intruders had keys (from Sheila's bag).
- Ross: Colonel Delaney drowned Nillebrook Water (~4 miles), foul play suspected, "Accidental death". Sir Matthew Fullgarney = key witness.
- Gossip: Sheila & Alan Warburton linked; cooled after Bank scandal.
- Postcard in scarf: "Dearest Sheila,—…the irides are simply wonderful." Signed "X". Postmark Dulwich (?). Handwriting slope unusual.
- Garage: **Standard** car. Bannister, Bathurst.

## Ch XI – Newspaper and Second Suit-Case
- Hood and side-screens up; no petrol to speak of.
- Second suit-case "S.D." under rear seat.
- Newspaper in dashboard pigeonhole: **Seabourne Herald, Thursday July 5th** (only sold in Seabourne).
- Bannister wires Otterton (Ross). Old companion: "Carr" name slip.
- Bathurst: "Who is 'X'?" Handwriting resembles something he has seen.
- Godfrey was to trace purchase of hydrocyanic acid (poisons book signature).
- Bathurst & Bannister stay at **The Grand**, Westhampton. Two young commercials **Rogers and Davidson** in corner overhear "Alan Warburton", "Daphne Carruthers".

## Ch XII – Local Gossip
- Bannister: "friends of young Warburton behind".
- **Falcon**, proprietor of Grand Hotel. Tells of Carruthers murder rumour.
- Falcon: Sheila and Alan "great friends", less intimate lately; Sheila other admirers unknown.
- Rogers & Davidson: Alan Warburton "Bolshie" after Sir Felix; vowed revenge on a "Prince" (boiling oil; "reminded me of geraniums"). Bannister: "the Crown Prince of Clorania?" Davidson: "you've holed in one".

## Ch XIII – Re-enter Mr. X
- **Pinkie (Agnes Kerr)**, ~60s, Devon/Scots; Colonel Dan's household; grief.
- Alan Warburton stopped visiting after Hunt Ball last February.
- Sheila "needed putting in his place".
- Secret letters/postcards in unknown hand, initial "X"; first about Eastertide (Maundy Thursday) last year.
- Sheila kept small right-hand drawer locked.
- Sheila went to London ~6 times in last year.
- Indian visitor ~a month ago: **Lal Singh**, Colonel's former body-servant; asked for Sir Matthew & Major Carruthers; Sheila gave money; spoke Hindustani wrong dialect (per later).
- Pinkie to stay with Lucas, **21 Crossley Road, Westhampton**.
- Bathurst's envelope address written by Pinkie; handwriting matches "X" card slope.

## Ch XIV – The Peacock's Eye
- **E. Kingsley Stark**, Manager, Westhampton branch, Mutual Bank (since May last year; about 14 months; rumoured connections).
- Cashier **Churchill**: Sheila cashed £100 cheque Thursday (5 × £10, 8 × £5, rest currency).
- Stark: Sheila requested **"The Peacock's Eye"** (blue-shaded emerald, ~£20,000) from private safe deposit; signed receipt; took it.
- Bannister: "Juno… hundred eyes of Argus".
- Letter from Stark to police; meeting at Grand Hotel, 11:30. Bathurst notes "E.K.S." (= "X" as pronounced).
- Falcon: "Mr. Alan Warburton" downstairs.

## Ch XV – Alan Warburton Leads Trumps
- Warburton unshaven, dishevelled, wild-eyed.
- Claims: loved Sheila; met "Alexis" (Crown Prince) at Hunt Ball in Feb last year, introduced by Major Carruthers; Sheila later told him; Crown Prince "murderer".
- Bannister: Crown Prince was at Seabourne with Daphne.
- Warburton stayed at **"Sea View", Mrs. Leach's boarding-house, Froam Road, Seabourne** (3 miles from sea).
- Bannister reveals Willoughby's notes traced. (Bannister's reference to notes telephoned to him at Grand Hotel: "two fives and a ten".)

## Ch XVI – Of Which Mr. Bathurst Holds the Ace
- Bannister leaves Westhampton next morning.
- Bathurst's "Initial Summary of Facts" (A–M): Hunt Ball attendees; Cassandra photo; Seabourne; suit-case substitution; poisoning at dentist's; lover; correspondence; Lal Singh; Willoughby; Stark; "X" in the Dulwich postcard; (M) did Stark know Sir Felix Warburton?
- Bathurst visits **19 Crossley Road**; slatternly woman; claims "Mr. Bannister's assistant".
- Bathurst reveals he acts for Crown Prince; shows blackmail letters. Warburton admits blackmail: "I knew he'd been meeting her." Bathurst promises no prosecution on Crown Prince's behalf.
- Bathurst asks Sir Matthew's address: **Dovaston Court**, two miles out on Bedford Road.

## Ch XVII – Bannister Strikes the Trail
- Bannister returns to Seabourne.
- Godfrey: Seabourne Southern & Home Counties Bank cashier; two £5 notes paid into **Cassandra** account by **Captain Willoughby** (weekly account).
- Willoughby: cousin **Phipps-Holloway**, racehorse trainer; colt **"Sherlock Holmes"** (by Hurry On, out of Popingaol) at Newmarket First July Meeting; tip from cousin "Lobster"; £10 stake → £50 winnings paid in cash by bookmaker **Jacob Morley, 9 Macbeth Court Mansions, Seabourne**.
- Godfrey: Morley = Branston's appointment at 2:30.

## Ch XVIII – Round the Mulberry-Bush
- Macbeth Court Mansions; Morley's maid; Morley's pompous speech.
- Morley: didn't keep appointment (two clerks away); visited Branston Saturday for teeth.
- Bannister shows note numbers; one £5 note = one of stolen notes.
- Morley: received notes from **Ronald Branston** (settling account) and paid them to Willoughby. (Branston had a "system" losing money on bets.)

## Ch XIX – Ronald Branston's Story
- Godfrey: Mrs. Bertenshaw widow; son abroad (India/Calcutta); maiden name **Warrimore**.
- Godfrey's theory: Mrs. Bertenshaw could have bolted door.
- Bannister wonders why poison-murder would need staged imprisonment.
- Godfrey: suicides don't have teeth pulled / hair-cut.
- Fingerprints: bolt → Mrs. B & Branston; glass → Branston & Delaney.
- Branston's library. Bannister: Sheila robbed of £100 and Peacock's Eye.
- Branston admits: notes came from Mrs. Bertenshaw who repaid him £50 (he had lent her £50 a year ago).

## Ch XX – "Findings—Keepings"
- Bannister accuses Branston/Mrs B; Mrs B tearfully: found £100 in notes in **art-pot** in hall (~5pm, murder afternoon); kept part; repaid Branston £50.
- Bannister: "Supposing murderer wanted something… couldn't get without first taking notes."

## Ch XXI – Lord Lieutenant Goes Back a Few Years
- Bathurst at Dovaston Court with Sir Matthew (blue eyes, white moustache, pompous).
- Sir Matthew: Delaney, Carruthers and he were junior officers, **8th Westhampton Regiment**; sent to India; Baluchistan near Quetta, Bolan Pass.
- Temple "Sacred Peacock" (gold body, emerald eyes); the three entered at night; Delaney wrenched biggest emerald; lots drawn; Delaney won; kept till death.
- Lal Singh: Delaney's body-servant; father administered temple; guided them.
- Bathurst: Lal Singh visited Sheila recently (Pinkie's story); Sir Matthew never saw him.
- Sir Felix's suicide on the day of the Hunt Ball (per Sir Matthew).

## Ch XXII – Gallant Mr. Bathurst
- Lady Pauline Fullgarney: Crown Prince introduced at Hunt Ball; he danced with **Daphne** a lot; she never recalls him with Sheila.
- Banter ("Irish", "flair for selection").

## Ch XXIII – Mr. Bathurst Forgets His Change
- Crown Prince visits Bathurst (Falcon announces).
- Bathurst: letters handled; no prosecution; Alan Warburton the blackmailer; Sheila/Prince story "a mix-up"; Crown Prince denies ever meeting Sheila.
- Bathurst to **Pinkie** at 21 Crossley Road: Lal Singh spoke English; Sheila spoke Hindustani (wrong dialect).
- Editor of **Westhampton and Chellingborough Independent**: Feb 19 issue—Sir Felix arrested Wednesday at **Wyvenhoe Towers, Nillebrook**. Bathurst leaves 10s note for a Guinness without change.

## Ch XXIV – What Did Mr. Bathurst Whisper?
- Sir Austin Kemble, Brigadier-General, K.C.V.O., D.S.O., Commissioner. "Daily Bugle" attack (Wokingham Wheelbarrow, Leighton Buzzard moneylender cases).
- Bannister's report. Bannister suggests arresting Branston/Mrs B.
- Fences: **Levigne and Kharkoff (Paris), Stefanopoulos (Amsterdam), Schneitzer (London)**.
- Bathurst: "perhaps" Bannister's report; claims he'll wait for murderer's mistake.
- Bathurst whispers murderer's name to Bannister (Bannister: "Never!").

## Ch XXV – Patience Rewarded
- Months pass (July→Oct). Bannister retires (Sir Austin's farewell); Bathurst's letter to Bannister ("Hold yourself in readiness…").
- Mid-November: **S.S. Nicholas Maes** (Holland S.S. Co.) Hull→Amsterdam. Bannister as "Hobbs"/"Sutcliffe"-style aliases; Lal Singh as "Ram Das".
- Aeroplane carries Sir Austin, Crown Prince, Bathurst to Amsterdam; Kalverstraat; **Café Suisse**.
- **Cuypers**, head of Dutch police.
- Stefanopoulos: "Demetri"; one of three biggest fences; Jewish Quarter; registered moneylender; Greek father diamond-cutter (Zwanenburger Straat). Cuypers threatens: **Contessa D'Amaldi's nine pigeon-blood rubies**.

## Ch XXVI – Rendezvous
- Trap in Demetri's shop; Cuypers with Smith & Wesson; watchers behind door.
- 5pm: Lal Singh arrives; shows Peacock's Eye; Demetri examines.
- Bathurst & Cuypers arrest Lal Singh: "for the murder of Sheila Delaney at Seabourne… July fifth".
- Bathurst pulls beard off → reveals **Bannister** (no beard, same face, reveals identity).

## Ch XXVII – Sir Austin Kemble Removes His Hat
- Christmas dinner at Dovaston Court (Sir Matthew, Lady Pauline, Lady Brantwood, Sir Austin, Lady Kemble, Bathurst).
- Trial concluded; "jury absent 25 minutes"; sentence "Three Sundays" (hanging implied).
- Crown Prince's wedding fixed for last day of the old year.
- Bathurst's full explanation: Bannister (Chief-Inspector; Hunt Ball as "Mr. X"; in love with Sheila); Crown Prince mistaken as "Alexis" by Warburton; Bannister's motive—Peacock's Eye and avoiding exposure; retirement pressure. Poisoned Sheila with syringe; stole Daphne's suit-case; booked "Lauderdale"; drove Sheila's car back to Tranfield; caught 7:04 train; alibi via Willoughby. Clues: spectacles, "irides" plural, "data" plural, postcard in scarf, "Kerr" pronunciation, Dulwich postmark.
- Bathurst reveals: whispered **Sir Matthew Fullgarney's** name to Bannister (the wrong name, as a bluff). Sir Matthew asks; Bathurst confirms.
- Lady Fullgarney's musical laugh. **The End.**

## Transcriber's Note
- Corrections: misplaced quote marks (4); "replys"→"replies" (Ch V); "Cuypers white teeth"→"Cuypers' white teeth" (Ch XXV); "Cuyper's face"→"Cuypers' face" (Ch XXVI).
